statusText: Early U.S. afternoon (about three hours after cash open, roughly 12:36pm ET): today's confirmed UMich consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM) remain fully priced, with real-time index-level reporting mixed but consistently sub-0.5% in either direction (some sources show Dow/Nasdaq slightly negative, others show a modest Nasdaq gain) rather than a confirmed directional break, a day after Thursday's record S&P 500 close above 7,800. NQ futures continue trading inside the same broad range flagged across recent runs -- today's confirmed session range 30,124.25-30,232.00, with a later GEX/options-flow snapshot near 30,263.62 carrying some timestamp/source uncertainty since it sits slightly above the stated high -- still under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall. VIX holds calm near 14.63 (range 14.39-14.80); no fresher intraday print was confirmed this hour. 2Y/10Y Treasury yields (4.20%/4.68%) and QQQ ($732.07) remain unchanged from Alpha Vantage's stale prior reads (dated August 12-13); WTI ($84.77) and Brent ($93.26) similarly returned the same stale August 11 values. Fresher WebSearch reporting shows oil little changed today (WTI ~$81.24, Brent ~$87.02) after an early spike (Brent to ~$87.31, WTI to ~$81.83) faded, following confirmation that two tankers were attacked transiting the Strait of Hormuz Thursday evening (ADNOC said two of its vessels were hit, blaming Iran) and that transit has since ground to a near standstill; the U.S. reiterated it can maintain its naval blockade of Iranian ports 'indefinitely,' and Treasury Secretary Bessent warned of unprecedented 'economic isolation' measures against Iran. This is an incremental escalation in confirmed facts and rhetoric versus the prior run, but it has not produced a fresh directional break in oil or equities. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD, GLOBAL_QUOTE, WTI and BRENT calls all succeeded this run but returned unchanged stale prints; MARKET_STATUS failed twice with Cloudflare 502 gateway errors and was not pursued further (U.S. market-open status confirmed instead via WebSearch reporting of live intraday trading). Live VIX, NQ intraday levels, the Hormuz tanker-attack detail, and equity-market context all came from WebSearch.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail holds low because NQ itself continues to show no persistent one-way structure -- futures remain inside the same broad range flagged across recent runs, and today's confirmed data misses plus the incremental Hormuz tanker-attack/blockade rhetoric have not produced a failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in the index. Stress eases only modestly from the prior run's local high and stays in the upper-moderate band: the confirmed UMich miss is further behind the tape, but the newly confirmed tanker attacks and 'near standstill' Hormuz transit are a genuine, if not yet price-transmitting, escalation that keeps event-importance and surprise-magnitude drivers elevated. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself -- not the standing data misses, the Hormuz rhetoric/tanker attacks on their own, or any single-stock catalyst.
headline: Confirmed UMich miss and already-absorbed Retail Sales drop stay fully priced with only a mixed, sub-0.5% cross-index reaction; NQ holds its established range as reports confirm two tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and transit has ground to a near standstill, though oil (WTI ~$81.24, Brent ~$87.02) and VIX (~14.63) remain little changed after an early spike faded.
body: At 16:36 UTC, roughly three hours after the U.S. cash open, the confirmed August University of Michigan consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM vs +0.1% expected, steepest since May 2025) remain fully digested. Real-time index-level reporting is mixed and imprecise across sources this hour -- one snapshot shows the S&P 500 up 0.08%, the Dow off 0.13% and the Nasdaq up 0.17%, while another shows the Dow and Nasdaq Composite each modestly lower -- but all readings are consistently sub-0.5% in either direction, consistent with continued contained digestion rather than a confirmed directional break, a day after Thursday's record S&P 500 close above 7,800. NQ futures remain within the same broad range flagged across recent runs: today's confirmed session range is 30,124.25-30,232.00, with a later GEX/options-flow snapshot near 30,263.62 (sitting slightly above the stated session high, so carrying some timestamp/source uncertainty as in prior runs) still comfortably under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall. VIX remains calm, last confirmed near 14.63 (range 14.39-14.80); no fresher intraday print could be confirmed via available sources this hour. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD calls (2Y 4.20%, 10Y 4.68%, both dated August 12), GLOBAL_QUOTE (QQQ $732.07, dated August 13), WTI ($84.77) and BRENT ($93.26, both dated August 11) all succeeded this run but returned the identical stale values already published in prior runs -- no fresher daily print has posted yet on the free tier. MARKET_STATUS failed twice with transient Cloudflare 502 gateway errors and was not pursued further per the economical-use instruction; U.S. market-open status was instead confirmed via WebSearch reporting of live intraday index and futures trading. Fresher WebSearch-sourced oil pricing shows WTI ~$81.24 and Brent ~$87.02, 'little changed' today after an early-session spike (Brent to ~$87.31, WTI to ~$81.83) faded; the spike followed confirmation that two tankers were attacked overnight transiting the Strait of Hormuz (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company said two of its vessels were hit Thursday evening, with the UAE government blaming Iran), and reporting now indicates transit through the strait has ground to a near standstill. The U.S. separately reiterated it can maintain its naval blockade of Iranian ports 'indefinitely,' and Treasury Secretary Bessent told Newsmax the administration is preparing 'economic isolation' measures against Iran 'never... seen' before. This is an incremental escalation in confirmed facts and rhetoric relative to the prior run's characterization, but oil has not broken out of its recent range and equities show no confirmed transmission, so it is treated as a Stress driver rather than a Tail driver this hour. In single-stock news, Reddit jumped roughly 10% on confirmation it will join the S&P 500 on August 18, and SanDisk rose about 7% after a bullish 2026 Investor Day outlook; neither is an index-level one-way catalyst. Tail holds at 8% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- NQ remains inside its established range despite two confirmed data misses and confirmed (if still contained) Hormuz tanker attacks, and the cross-index reaction stayed mixed and sub-0.5% rather than showing failed-pullback or repeated-extension behavior. Stress eases only modestly to 42% (moderate, upper band) from the prior run's 44% because, while the UMich/Retail Sales surprise is further behind the tape, the freshly confirmed tanker-attack and near-standstill Hormuz detail plus the more pointed 'economic isolation' rhetoric are genuine event-importance drivers that offset the natural decay from the data prints alone. Confidence holds near 52% (medium-low), roughly flat versus the prior run's 55%, reflecting continued strong WebSearch coverage of VIX, NQ range, the Hormuz specifics, oil, and equity commentary, offset by MARKET_STATUS failing twice, the Alpha Vantage yield/equity/oil series again returning no fresher information, and conflicting real-time percentage-move reporting across index-level sources this hour.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (8-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing steadily from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion into a stable single-digit floor through Friday's Asian/European session, then holding 8-9% into and through today's confirmed UMich and Retail Sales misses. Stress ran from the low-40s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, then rebuilt steadily through the European morning and into the confirmed UMich print, peaking at 44% before easing modestly to 42% as the data digested further into the U.S. early afternoon without a confirmed equity-market breakdown; the newly confirmed Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks add an incremental event-importance driver to the current read without yet showing price transmission into oil or equities.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-8%) through the next 24 hours as no confirmed persistent one-way NQ structure is in evidence and no further high-impact U.S. data is scheduled before the Friday close. Stress is projected to continue easing from today's local high in the low-40s as the UMich/Retail Sales data and the confirmed-but-contained Hormuz tanker-attack headlines are further digested through the remainder of the U.S. session, dropping into the low-double-digits by the ~21:00-22:00 UTC Friday close/CME weekend halt for NQ. From roughly 22:00 UTC Friday through the end of this forecast window (15:00 UTC Saturday), NQ futures are closed for the CME weekend break (reopening Sunday ~22:00 UTC), so Tail and Stress are held near a low weekend baseline reflecting the absence of active price-path evidence and standing weekend headline/gap risk (principally the Hormuz standoff) rather than any newly observed structure. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the low-50s toward the low-30s as the horizon moves away from this run's evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
